questions.q: What does the second law of thermodynamics state regarding thermal energy transfer and entropy?
a: Thermal energy can spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body without external work.
Total energy in any closed system is destroyed over time.

Thermal energy cannot spontaneously flow from a cooler body to a warmer body, and the total entropy of an isolated system always increases or remains constant in any spontaneous process.
